input:
The IT provider corpITOp requires a service to manage 5,000 office employees. This service must filter dangerous websites, 
scan downloaded files for malware, and ensure that sensitive data does not leave the network. The service chain begins by connecting a <webFilterVF, 4> 
allocated at the edge to a <malwareScannerVF, 16> located in the cloud; for this specific segment, it is mandatory that the latency remains below 10 milliseconds.
Subsequently, the chain proceeds by connecting the <malwareScannerVF, 16> to a <dlpEngineVF, 8> located in the cloud, ensuring a bandwidth greater than 500 mbps 
on this final link.

The media provider cinemaRenderOp requires a service to manage 5,000 rendering projects. This infrastructure receives raw digital scenes, 
distributes the rendering computation across hundreds of virtual nodes, and reassembles the finished frames for post-production. 
The service chain begins with a <sceneReceiverVF, 16> allocated at the edge. For this component, compression is applied after it. The chain 
then connects to an <assetValidatorVF, 12> located in the cloud followed by a <renderDistributorVF, 32> located in the cloud and a <frameAssemblerVF, 24> 
located in the cloud. For the entire deployment, it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 800 gb. Finally, 
the frames are routed to a <colorGraderVF, 20> located in the cloud, ensuring that caching is executed before it.

The media provider liveSubsOp requires a live subtitling service to manage 10,000 concurrent streams. This service intercepts the audio of a 
streaming event, transforms it into text via AI, translates it into three languages, and reinserts it into the video feed as subtitles. 
The service chain begins with an <audioExtractorVF, 8> allocated at the edge. For this component, caching is applied after it. The chain then 
connects to a <speechToTextVF, 32> located in the cloud followed by a <multiTranslatorVF, 24> located in the cloud. For the entire deployment, 
it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 100 gb. Finally, the text is routed to a <subtitleInjectorVF, 12> allocated 
at the edge, ensuring that the latency from the <speechToTextVF, 32> to this <subtitleInjectorVF, 12> must remain below 20 ms.

The enterprise provider corpDocOp requires a document classification engine to manage 50,000 daily files. This system analyzes PDF 
files or OCR scans, identifies the document type like invoice, contract, or reminder, and routes it to the competent business function. 
The service chain begins with an <ocrScannerVF, 16> allocated at the edge. For this component, security is applied after it. It is mandatory that 
this <ocrScannerVF, 16> and the next <textExtractorVF, 12>, located in the edge, are deployed on the same hosting node. The chain then connects to an <aiDocumentClassifierVF, 32> located in the cloud; for this connection, it is strictly required that the latency from the <textExtractorVF, 12> to the <aiDocumentClassifierVF, 32> 
remains below 50 ms. The chain proceeds to a <dataRedactorVF, 16> located in the cloud, ensuring that privacy is executed before it. Finally, the 
files are routed to a <documentRouterVF, 8> located in the cloud, and it is ideally preferred that the bandwidth from the <aiDocumentClassifierVF, 32> to this 
<documentRouterVF, 8> remains higher than 500 mbps.

The financial provider fraudSafeOp requires an antifraud analysis service to manage 200,000 transactions per hour. This system intercepts every digital payment 
request, compares it with habitual user spending patterns via machine learning, and authorizes the transaction in a few milliseconds. 
The service chain begins with a <requestInterceptorVF, 8> allocated at the edge. For this component, security is applied after it. It is mandatory that this <requestInterceptorVF, 8> and the next component, a <profileMatcherVF, 16>, operate on the same node at the edge. The chain then connects to an <mlAnalyzerVF, 32> located in the cloud, 
ensuring that privacy is executed before it. The chain then proceeds to a <policyEnforcerVF, 12> located in the cloud; it is ideally preferred that the bandwidth from 
the <mlAnalyzerVF, 32> to this <policyEnforcerVF, 12> remains higher than 1000 mbps. Finally, the system routes to a <responseEmitterVF, 8> located in the cloud, with a preference 
that the total chain hardware remains lower than 120 gb.

The financial provider hftGlobalOp requires a high frequency trading service to manage 500,000 orders. This infrastructure receives stock prices, 
executes decision algorithms, and sends purchase orders seeking the fastest network path. The service chain begins with a <marketFeedVF, 16> allocated at the edge. 
For this component, caching is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <tradingAlgoVF, 32> allocated at the edge, ensuring that it is mandatory for the latency 
from the <marketFeedVF, 16> to this <tradingAlgoVF, 32> to remain below 50 ms. The chain proceeds to a <riskCheckerVF, 16> located in the cloud; it is ideally preferred that the 
bandwidth from the <tradingAlgoVF, 32> to this <riskCheckerVF, 16> remains higher than 5000 mbps. Finally, the system routes to an <orderDispatcherVF, 8> allocated at the edge, 
with a preference that the latency from the <riskCheckerVF, 16> to this <orderDispatcherVF, 8> remains below 5 ms, and ensuring that logging is executed before it.

The financial provider onlineBankOp requires a digital identity verification service to manage 10,000 daily uploads. 
This service processes photos of documents uploaded by users, verifies their authenticity, and compares the data with international blacklists to prevent 
money laundering. The service chain begins with a <documentReceiverVF, 12> allocated at the edge. For this component, encoding is applied after it. The chain then 
connects to an <authenticityCheckerVF, 24> located in the cloud, ensuring that security is executed before it. The chain proceeds to an <amlMatcherVF, 16> located in the cloud; 
for this component, privacy is applied after it. Finally, the processed data is routed to a <profileCreatorVF, 16> located in the cloud, ensuring that compression 
is executed before it.

The service provider eInvoiceOp requires a digital invoicing service to manage 50,000 invoices per day. This system transforms sales data into certified XML files, 
applies the digital signature, and automatically sends them to governmental systems for fiscal validation. The service chain begins with a <saleDataCollectorVF, 8> 
allocated at the edge. For the entire deployment, it is mandatory that the total chain hardware remains lower than 150 gb. The chain then connects to an <xmlConverterVF, 16> located in the cloud. It is strictly required that the latency from this <xmlConverterVF, 16> to the next component, a <digitalSignerVF, 12> located in the cloud, 
remains below 30 ms. Finally, the files are routed to ataxAuthorityTransmitterVF located in the cloud, and it is ideally preferred that the bandwidth from the 
<digitalSignerVF, 12> to this <taxAuthorityTransmitterVF, 8> remains higher than 100 mbps.

The logistics provider deliveryLogisticsOp requires a route optimization service to manage 15,000 couriers. This software receives the GPS positions of a fleet, 
analyzes city traffic data, constantly recalculates the best route for each courier, and updates their terminals. The service chain begins with a <gpsIngesterVF, 8> 
allocated at the edge. For this component, compression is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <trafficAnalyzerVF, 24> located in the cloud followed by a 
<routeOptimizerVF, 32> located in the cloud. The updated routes are routed to a <terminalUpdaterVF, 12> allocated at the edge, ensuring that decoding is executed before it. 
For the entire deployment, it is strictly required that the latency from the begin to the end of the chain must remain below 80 ms.

The municipal provider smartParkOp requires a parking management backend to handle 100,000 active parking spots. This system receives occupancy alerts, 
updates the city map, and processes automatic payments. The service chain begins with a <sensorDataCollectorVF, 8> at the edge. For this component, compression 
is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <mapUpdaterVF, 16> in the cloud and a <paymentProcessorVF, 24> in the cloud; it is mandatory that these two VNF are deployed 
on dedicated nodes. Encoding is executed before the <paymentProcessorVF, 24>. The chain then connects to a <statusLoggerVF, 12> in the cloud, ensuring 
that logging is executed before it. Finally, the chain includes a <securityEnforcerVF, 16> in the cloud, with security applied after the <paymentProcessorVF, 24>. 
For the entire segment, it is strictly required that the latency from the <sensorDataCollectorVF, 8> to this <securityEnforcerVF, 16> remains below 30 ms.

The logistics provider aeroDeliveryOp requires a drone fleet control service to manage 5,000 active delivery drones. This system manages digital flight plans, 
avoids software collisions, and ensures that the command signal is always a priority. The service chain begins with a <flightTelemetryIngesterVF, 12> ingester allocated at the edge. 
For this component, caching is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <collisionAvoiderVF, 32> located in the cloud, ensuring that it is strictly required for the 
latency from the <flightTelemetryIngesterVF, 12> ingester to this <collisionAvoiderVF, 32> to remain below 10 ms. The chain proceeds to a <commandPrioritizerVF, 16> located in the cloud. 
Finally, the system routes to a <routeDispatcherVF, 12> allocated at the edge; it is ideally preferred that the bandwidth from the <collisionAvoiderVF, 32> to this <routeDispatcherVF, 12> remains higher than 2000 mbps. For the entire deployment, it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 200 gb.

The cybersecurity provider secureMailOp requires a service to manage 10,000 corporate mailboxes. This pipeline intercepts incoming emails, 
removes phishing links, analyzes attachments in an isolated environment, and delivers only safe messages to the server. The service chain begins 
with a <mailGatewayVF, 4> allocated at the edge. For this node, it is strictly required that decoding is applied after it. This <mailGatewayVF, 4> connects to a 
<phishingFilterVF, 8> located in the cloud, and for this link, it is ideally preferred that latency remains below 50 milliseconds. The chain then proceeds 
to a <sandboxScannerVF, 16> located in the cloud; between the filter and the scanner, it is mandatory to have a bandwidth higher than 100 Mbps. Additionally, 
logging must be enforced before the <sandboxScannerVF, 16>. Finally, the scanner connects to a <safeDeliveryVF, 4> node located in the cloud.

The infrastructure provider serverMonOp requires a telemetry monitoring service to manage 50,000 virtual machines. This service collects temperature, 
CPU load, and memory usage data, aggregating them to identify anomalies before failure occurs. The service chain begins with a <telemetryCollectorVF, 8> at the edge. 
It is mandatory that this <telemetryCollectorVF, 8> and the next component, a <dataAggregatorVF, 16> located in the edge, are deployed on the same hosting node. 
The chain then connects to ananomalyDetectorVF located in the cloud, and subsequently to an <alertDispatcherVF, 8> located in the cloud. Regarding constraints, 
it is strictly required that the latency from the begin to the end of the chain remains below 100 ms, and the provider ideally prefers that the bandwidth 
from the begin to the end of the chain remains higher than 2000 mbps.

The industrial provider autoWarehouseOp requires a remote control system for autonomous machines to manage 500 warehouse robots. 
This software receives sensor data, calculates paths to avoid collisions, and sends steering and braking commands. The service chain begins with a <sensorDataDecoderVF, 16> allocated at the edge. For this component, decoding is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <collisionPathSolverVF, 32> located in the cloud. 
Finally, the system routes to a <commandEncoderVF, 16> allocated at the edge, ensuring that encoding is executed before it. For the entire deployment, it is strictly 
required that the latency from the <sensorDataDecoderVF, 16> to this <commandEncoderVF, 16> remains below 500 ms.

The healthcare provider healthCareOp requires a post-operative tele-monitoring service to manage 5,000 active patients. This service receives digitalized patient 
vital data from home, analyzes cardiac anomalies, and notifies the doctor on duty immediately in case of danger. The service chain begins with a <patientDataReceiverVF, 8> allocated at the edge. For this component, privacy is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <cardiacAnomalyAnalyzerVF, 24> located in the cloud. 
The next component is a <medicalAlertLoggerVF, 12> located in the cloud, ensuring that logging is executed before it. Finally, the system routes to a <doctorNotifierVF, 8> 
located in the cloud, ensuring it is strictly required that the latency from the <patientDataReceiverVF, 8> to this <doctorNotifierVF, 8> remains below 100 ms. 
For the entire deployment, it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 80 gb.

The healthcare provider medDiagnosticOp requires a radiology AI diagnostics service to manage 10,000 daily scans. 
This pipeline receives high-resolution medical images, processes them with computer vision algorithms to highlight suspicious lesions, and stores them securely. 
The service chain begins with a <dicomIngesterVF, 16> allocated at the edge, specifying compression is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <lesionAnalyzerVF, 32> located in the cloud and a <metadataExtractorVF, 12> located in the cloud; for these two components, it is mandatory that they are isolated on dedicated hardware 
nodes, while ensuring the bandwidth from the <dicomIngesterVF, 16> to the <lesionAnalyzerVF, 32> remains higher than 500 mbps. Finally, the system routes the data to a secure 
<secureArchiverVF, 24> in the cloud, ensuring that data encoding is executed before it.

The digital provider secureVoteOp requires a certified electronic voting service to manage 200,000 voters. This platform for public or corporate consultations 
guarantees vote anonymity and prevents data manipulation. The service chain begins with a <ballotIngesterVF, 12> allocated at the edge. The chain then connects 
to an <anonymizerVoteVF, 16> located in the cloud, ensuring that the network bandwidth from the <ballotIngesterVF, 12> to this <anonymizerVoteVF, 16> remains higher than 
100 mbps, while privacy is applied after it. The pipeline continues to an <integrityEnforcerVF, 24> located in the cloud, ensuring that security is executed before it. 
The system then routes the data to a <voteCounterVF, 16> located in the cloud. Finally, the processed data flows to an <electoralAuditLoggerVF, 12> located in the cloud, ensuring 
that logging is executed before it.

The digital provider govDataOp requires an open data portal service to manage 30,000 dataset downloads per day. This system extracts datasets from public databases, 
normalizes them into open formats, adds search metadata, and makes them available for public download. The service chain begins with a <dataExtractorVF, 8> 
allocated at the edge. The chain then connects to a <formatNormalizerVF, 16> located in the cloud, specifying that data caching is applied after it. 
The next component is a <metadataEnricherVF, 12> located in the cloud; it is mandatory that this <formatNormalizerVF, 16> and the <metadataEnricherVF, 12> are hosted 
together on the exact same physical server, while preferring that the network bandwidth between them remains higher than 1000 mbps. Finally, 
the system routes the files to a <downloadProviderVF, 16> located in the cloud, ensuring that the total latency from the initial <dataExtractorVF, 8> to 
this final <downloadProviderVF, 16> is strictly required to remain below 200 ms.

The educational provider eduCloudOp requires a virtual student lab platform to support 10,000 concurrent students. This system provides temporary programming 
environments, manages resource allocation for each student, and monitors the workspaces to prevent improper use. The service chain begins with a <sessionIngesterVF, 8> allocated at the edge, data privacy mechanisms are applied after it. The system then connects to a <resourceAllocatorVF, 16> located in the cloud, ensuring that the network capacity between the <sessionIngesterVF, 8> and this <resourceAllocatorVF, 16> supports more than 500 mbps. 
The pipeline continues to an <activityMonitorVF, 24> located in the cloud, ensuring that security are executed before it, and that the latency time 
from the <sessionIngesterVF, 8> to this <activityMonitorVF, 24> is kept under 40 ms. The next blocks are a <userPrivacyEnforcerVF, 12> located in the cloud and an <auditLoggerVF, 12> 
located in the cloud, where logging are executed before the <auditLoggerVF, 12>. Finally, the system routes the results to an <outputPackagerVF, 16> located in the cloud, 
specifying that compression is applied after it. For the whole deployment, the provider prefers that the aggregate infrastructure footprint stays below 120 gb.

The marketing provider sentimentOp requires a customer sentiment analysis platform to manage 100,000 daily reviews and comments. This software scans social media 
inputs, identifies prevailing emotions toward specific products, and sends weekly reports to the marketing department. The service chain begins with a <socialDataReceiverVF, 16> allocated at the edge, specifying that data privacy mechanisms are applied after it. The chain then connects to a <sentimentAnalyzerVF, 32> in the cloud, 
ensuring that security is executed before this component. Finally, the pipeline routes to a <reportDispatcherVF, 16> located in the cloud, mandating that this 
<reportDispatcherVF, 16> and the previous <sentimentAnalyzerVF, 32> are hosted together on the same physical infrastructure.

The industrial provider factoryCloudOp requires an augmented reality back-end service to support 500 active smart glasses on the shop floor. 
This service sends visual technical instructions to workers' headsets, overlaying maintenance data on the framed machinery in real time. 
The service chain begins with an <arStreamReceiverVF, 12> allocated at the edge. The chain then connects to <arPoseEstimatorVF, 24> located in the 
cloud and a <dataOverlayEngineVF, 32> located in the cloud; for these two intensive blocks, it is mandatory that they are isolated on dedicated hardware nodes, 
while ensuring that the network bandwidth between the initial <arStreamReceiverVF, 12> and the <arPoseEstimatorVF, 24> remains higher than 200 mbps. Finally, the system 
routes the processed graphics to an <arStreamDispatcherVF, 16> located in the cloud, ensuring it is strictly required that the latency from the <arStreamReceiverVF, 12> 
to this <arStreamDispatcherVF, 16> remains below 12 ms. For the overall infrastructure, it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 90 gb.

The digital provider subscriptionOp requires a SaaS subscription management service to manage 50,000 active accounts. This recurring billing service handles 
customer payment cycles, software plan upgrades, and automated reminders for expired credit cards. The service chain begins with a <subscriptionIngesterVF, 12> allocated 
at the edge, ensuring that customer privacy is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <billingCycleProcessorVF, 24> located in the cloud, specifying that 
decoding is executed before it to parse incoming payment tokens. The next component is a <dunningManagerVF, 16> located in the cloud, ensuring that transaction logging 
is executed before it to catch failure triggers. Finally, the system routes the billing results to an <invoiceGeneratorVF, 16> located in the cloud, where data encoding 
is executed before it for secure document delivery.

The website security provider ddosProtectionOp requires an anti-DDoS defense system to handle 50,000 active web users. 
This system analyzes incoming traffic, cleans malicious flows, and ensures server availability. The service chain starts with a <networkTrafficAnalyzerVF, 8> located at the edge. 
A bandwidth higher than 500 megabps is strictly required from this <networkTrafficAnalyzerVF, 8> to a <scrubbingFilterVF, 32> located in the cloud. For this <scrubbingFilterVF, 32>, it is mandatory 
that security is executed before it. The chain then connects to a <rateLimiterVF, 16> located in the cloud. It is ideally preferred that logging is applied after 
the <rateLimiterVF, 16>. Finally, the traffic is directed to a <webServerVF, 12> located in the cloud, where a latency lower than 10 ms is desired between the <rateLimiterVF, 16> 
and the <webServerVF, 12>.

The software provider devToolsOp requires a code efficiency analyzer service to manage 20,000 daily evaluation requests. This platform receives code snippets, 
executes a simulated runtime execution, and suggests specific optimizations to reduce computational resource consumption. The service chain begins with a <codeReceiverVF, 8> allocated at the edge, which handles the initial incoming snippets. The chain then connects to a <syntaxValidatorVF, 12> located in the cloud, ensuring that 
data caching is applied after it. The pipeline continues to a <sandboxSimulatorVF, 32> located in the cloud and an <optimizationEngineVF, 24> located in the cloud to evaluate 
runtime performance. Finally, the system routes the generated insights to a <developersReportGeneratorVF, 16> located in the cloud, specifying that data compression is applied after it. 
For the whole cluster deployment, it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 110 gb.

The compliance provider gdprComplianceOp requires a GDPR verification service to manage 5,000 corporate database connections. This service scans corporate
databases to identify unprotected personal data, applies automatic anonymization, and generates reports for regulators. The service chain begins with a 
<dbScannerVF, 16> allocated at the edge. For this component, privacy must be applied after it. The <dbScannerVF, 16> connects to an <anonymizerVF, 24> located in the cloud, 
and for this connection, it is ideally preferred that latency remains lower than 20 ms. The chain then proceeds to a <reportGeneratorVF, 8> located in the cloud; 
between the <anonymizerVF, 24> and the <reportGeneratorVF, 8>, it is mandatory to have a bandwidth higher than 50 Mbps. Additionally, security must be enforced before the report <reportGeneratorVF, 8>.

The network security provider secureCryptoOp requires an encrypted traffic analysis service to support 25,000 corporate users. This service inspects HTTPS flows 
without fully decrypting them, using AI to identify malware or botnet patterns. The service chain begins with a <trafficSplitterVF, 8> allocated at the edge. For this 
component, decoding is applied after it. It is mandatory that this <trafficSplitterVF, 8> and the next <featureExtractorVF, 16>, located in the edge, are deployed on the same 
hosting node. The chain then proceeds to an <aiClassifierVF, 32> located in the cloud, followed by an <alertManagerVF, 4> located in the cloud. For the entire deployment, it is 
ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 80 gigabytes. Finally, the traffic is routed to a <policyEnforcerVF, 12> located in the cloud, ensuring 
that security is executed before the <policyEnforcerVF, 12>.

The government provider govMessagingOp requires a service to manage 50,000 institutional messages. This service receives digital communications, 
verifies the electronic signature of the sender, checks its integrity, and archives the message in a legal vault. The service chain begins with 
a <msgReceiverVF, 8> allocated at the edge. For this component, caching is applied after it. The chain connects to a <sigVerifierVF, 16> located in 
the cloud. It is strictly required that this <sigVerifierVF, 16> and the next component, an <integrityCheckerVF, 12> located in the cloud, are deployed 
on the same hosting node. For the entire deployment, it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 100 gb. Finally, 
the messages are routed to a <legalVaultVF, 32> located in the cloud, ensuring that compression is executed before it.

Cloud gaming service provider GamingOp needs a service to handle 40,000 active players. This service runs games on powerful servers and 
streams the video to the user, ensuring very low latency to prevent the game from becoming unplayable. The service chain begins with a 
<gameExecutorVF, 32> hosted in the cloud. Encoding is applied after to this component. Ideally, this <gameExecutorVF, 32> is preferred to run on a dedicated node. 
The chain then connects to a <streamPackerVF, 16> hosted in the cloud; this component is also preferred to run on a dedicated node. Finally, 
the traffic is routed to a <deliveryOptimizerVF, 8> hosted at the edge, ensuring that the latency from the <streamPackerVF, 16> to this <deliveryOptimizerVF, 8> remains less than 30 ms.

The media provider mediaBroadcastOp requires a live multicamera streaming service to support 30,000 concurrent viewers. 
This system receives video streams from different angles, allows cloud mixing, adds advertising graphics, and distributes the signal to 
thousands of viewers simultaneously. The service chain begins with a <streamIngesterVF, 12> allocated at the edge. For this component, 
compression is applied after it. The chain then connects to a <cloudStudioVF, 32> located in the cloud followed by a <graphicInjectorVF, 16> located in the 
cloud. Between this <graphicInjectorVF, 16> and the next component, it is strictly required to maintain a bandwidth higher than 5000 mbps. Finally, 
the traffic is routed to a <streamDistributorVF, 24> located in the cloud, ensuring that caching is executed before it. For the entire deployment, 
it is ideally preferred that the total chain hardware remains lower than 150 gb.

The media provider vodStreamOp requires a video on demand distribution service to manage 80,000 active subscribers. 
This service optimizes movie delivery by encrypting content with DRM, compressing it into different formats, and storing it on nodes 
close to the user to avoid buffering. The service chain begins with a <drmEncryptorVF, 16> allocated in the cloud. For this component, encoding 
is applied after it. It is ideally preferred that this <drmEncryptorVF, 16> and the next component, a <transcoderVF, 32> allocated in the cloud, 
are deployed on the same hosting node. The chain then proceeds to a <cachingNodeVF, 12> node allocated at the edge; between the <transcoderVF, 32> and 
this <cachingNodeVF, 12> node, it is strictly required to maintain a bandwidth higher than 10000 mbps. Additionally, decoding must be executed 
before the <cachingNodeVF, 12> node.
